exercises.heading: 13.4. Exercises

problem.paragraph: The table gives coordinates of a particle moving through space along a smooth curve.

list.item: Find the average velocities over the time intervals $$\lbrack 0,1\rbrack$$ , $$\lbrack 0.5,1\rbrack$$ , $$\lbrack 1,2\rbrack$$ , and $$\lbrack 1,1.5\rbrack$$ .

problem.paragraph: The figure shows the path of a particle that moves with position vector $$\mathbf{r}{(t)}$$ at time $$t$$ .

list.item: Draw a vector that represents the average velocity of the particle over the time interval $$2 \leqslant t \leqslant 2.4$$ .
Draw a vector that represents the average velocity over the time interval $$1.5 \leqslant t \leqslant 2$$ .
Write an expression for the velocity vector $$\mathbf{v}{(2)}$$ .

Draw an approximation to the vector $$\mathbf{v}{(2)}$$ and estimate the speed of the particle at $$t = 2$$ . Details A curve and three vectors are graphed in the x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes are displayed from 0 to 2 in increments of 1. The curve enters from the bottom right, goes steeply upward to the left, concave down, and runs almost horizontally to the left, initially concave down and then becomes concave up, crosses the y axis at approximately (0, 3.5), and exits at the top left of the viewing window. An arrow placed on the curve indicates the direction of its path. All three vectors begin from the origin. The first vector is labeled vector r(2, 4), slopes slightly steeply upward to the right, and meets the curve as it begins to run horizontally. The second vector, labeled vector r(2), slopes upward to the right and meets the curve as it turns. The third vector, labeled vector r(1, 5), slopes gradually upward to the right and meets the curve as it ascends.

exercises.instruction: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 Find the velocity, acceleration, and speed of a particle with the given position function. Sketch the path of the particle and draw the velocity and acceleration vectors for the specified value of $$t$$ .

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {\langle{- \frac{1}{2}t^{2},t}\rangle}$$ , $$t = 2$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {\langle{t^{2},1 \slash t^{2}}\rangle}$$ , $$t = 1$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = 3\cos t\mathbf{i} + 2\sin t\mathbf{j}$$ , $$t = \pi \slash 3$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = e^{ t}\mathbf{i} + e^{2t}\mathbf{j}$$ , $$t = 0$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = t\mathbf{i} + t^{2}\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$$ , $$t = 1$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = t\mathbf{i} + 2\cos t\mathbf{j} + \sin t\mathbf{k}$$ , $$t = 0$$

exercises.instruction: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14 Find the velocity, acceleration, and speed of a particle with the given position function.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {\langle{t^{2} + t,t^{2} - t,t^{3}}\rangle}$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {\langle{2\cos t,3t,2\sin t}\rangle}$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = \sqrt{2}t\mathbf{i} + e^{ t}\mathbf{j} + e^{- t}\mathbf{k}$$

solution.paragraph: $$\sqrt{2}\mathbf{i} + e^{ t}\mathbf{j} - e^{- t}\mathbf{k}$$ , $$e^{ t}\mathbf{j} + e^{- t}\mathbf{k}$$ , $$e^{ t} + e^{- t}$$

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = t^{2}\mathbf{i} + 2t\mathbf{j} + \ln t\mathbf{k}$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = e^{ t}{({\cos t\mathbf{i} + \sin t\mathbf{j} + t\mathbf{k}})}$$

solution.paragraph: $$e^{ t}\left\lbrack {({\cos t - \sin t})\mathbf{i} + {({\sin t + \cos t})}\mathbf{j} + {({t + 1})}\mathbf{k}} \right\rbrack$$ , $$e^{ t}\lbrack - 2\sin t\mathbf{i} + 2\cos\mathbf{t}\mathbf{j} + (t + 2)\mathbf{k}\rbrack$$ , $$e^{ t}\sqrt{t^{2} + 2t + 3}$$

problem.paragraph: $${\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {\langle{t^{2},\sin t - t\cos t,\cos t + t\sin t}\rangle}}, {t \geqslant 0}$$

exercises.instruction: 15–16 Find the velocity and position vectors of a particle that has the given acceleration and the given initial velocity and position.

problem.paragraph: $$a{(t)} = 2\mathbf{i} + 2t\mathbf{k}$$ , $$\mathbf{v}{(0)} = 3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}$$ , $$\mathbf{r}{(0)} = \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$$
$$a{(t)} = \sin t\mathbf{i} + 2\cos t\mathbf{j} + 6t\mathbf{k}$$ , $$\mathbf{v}{(0)} = - \mathbf{k}$$ , $$\mathbf{r}{(0)} = \mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k}$$

exercises.instruction: 17–18 Find the position vector of a particle that has the given acceleration and the specified initial velocity and position. Graph the path of the particle.

problem.paragraph: $$a{(t)} = 2t\mathbf{i} + \sin t\mathbf{j} + \cos 2t\mathbf{k}$$ , $$\mathbf{v}{(0)} = \mathbf{i}$$ , $$\mathbf{r}{(0)} = \mathbf{j}$$
$$a{(t)} = t\mathbf{i} + e^{ t}\mathbf{j} + e^{- t}\mathbf{k}$$ , $$\mathbf{v}{(0)} = \mathbf{k}$$ , $$\mathbf{r}{(0)} = \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$$
The position function of a particle is given by $$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {\langle{t^{2},5t,t^{2} - 16t}\rangle}$$ . When is the speed a minimum?
What force is required so that a particle of mass $$m$$ has the position function $$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = t^{3}\mathbf{i} + t^{2}\mathbf{j} + t^{3}\mathbf{k}$$ ?

A force with magnitude $$20$$ N acts directly upward from the $$xy$$ -plane on an object with mass $$4$$ kg. The object starts at the origin with initial velocity $$\mathbf{v}{(0)} = \mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}$$ . Find its position function and its speed at time $$t$$ .
Show that if a particle moves with constant speed, then the velocity and acceleration vectors are orthogonal.
A projectile is fired with an initial speed of $$200m \slash s$$ and angle of elevation $$60^{{^\circ}}$$ . Find
Rework Exercise 23 if the projectile is fired from a position $$100$$ m above the ground.
A ball is thrown upward at an angle of $$45^{{^\circ}}$$ to the ground. If the ball lands $$90$$ m away, what was the initial speed of the ball?
A projectile is fired from a tank with initial speed $$400m \slash s$$ . Find two angles of elevation that can be used to hit a target $$3000$$ m away.
A rifle is fired with angle of elevation $$36^{{^\circ}}$$ . What is the initial speed if the maximum height of the bullet is $$1600$$ ft?

A batter hits a baseball $$3$$ ft above the ground toward the center field fence, which is $$10$$ ft high and $$400$$ ft from home plate. The ball leaves the bat with speed $$115{ft} \slash s$$ at an angle $$50^{{^\circ}}$$ above the horizontal. Is it a home run? (In other words, does the ball clear the fence?)

A medieval city has the shape of a square and is protected by walls with length $$500$$ m and height $$15$$ m. You are the commander of an attacking army and the closest you can get to the wall is $$100$$ m. Your plan is to set fire to the city by catapulting heated rocks over the wall (with an initial speed of $$80m \slash s$$ ). At what range of angles should you tell your men to set the catapult? (Assume the path of the rocks is perpendicular to the wall.)
Show that a projectile reaches three-quarters of its maximum height in half the time needed to reach its maximum height.

A ball is thrown eastward into the air from the origin (in the direction of the positive $$x$$ -axis). The initial velocity is $$50\mathbf{i} + 80\mathbf{k}$$ , with speed measured in feet per second. The spin of the ball results in a southward acceleration of $$4{ft} \slash s^{2}$$ , so the acceleration vector is $$a = - 4\mathbf{j} - 32\mathbf{k}$$ . Where does the ball land and with what speed?

A ball with mass $$0.8$$ kg is thrown southward into the air with a speed of $$30m \slash s$$ at an angle of $$30^{{^\circ}}$$ to the ground. A west wind applies a steady force of $$4$$ N to the ball in an easterly direction. Where does the ball land and with what speed?

Water traveling along a straight portion of a river normally flows fastest in the middle, and the speed slows to almost zero at the banks. Consider a long straight stretch of river flowing north, with parallel banks $$40$$ m apart. If the maximum water speed is $$3m \slash s$$ , we can use a quadratic function as a basic model for the rate of water flow $$x$$ units from the west bank: $$f{(x)} = \frac{3}{400}x{({40 - x})}$$ .

list.item: A boat proceeds at a constant speed of $$5m \slash s$$ from a point $$A$$ on the west bank while maintaining a heading perpendicular to the bank. How far down the river on the opposite bank will the boat touch shore? Graph the path of the boat.

Suppose we would like to pilot the boat to land at the point $$B$$ on the east bank directly opposite $$A$$ . If we maintain a constant speed of $$5m \slash s$$ and a constant heading, find the angle at which the boat should head. Then graph the actual path the boat follows. Does the path seem realistic?

problem.paragraph: Another reasonable model for the water speed of the river in Exercise 33 is a sine function: $$f{(x)} = 3\sin{({\pi x \slash 40})}$$ . If a boater would like to cross the river from $$A$$ to $$B$$ with constant heading and a constant speed of $$5m \slash s$$ , determine the angle at which the boat should head.
A particle has position function $$\mathbf{r}{(t)}$$ . If $$\mathbf{r}^{\prime}{(t)} = \mathbf{c} \times \mathbf{r}{(t)}$$ , where $$c$$ is a constant vector, describe the path of the particle.

solution.paragraph: The path is contained in a circle that lies in a plane perpendicular to $$\mathbf{c}$$ with center on a line through the origin in the direction of $$\mathbf{c}$$ .

list.item: If a particle moves along a straight line, what can you say about its acceleration vector?
If a particle moves with constant speed along a curve, what can you say about its acceleration vector?

exercises.instruction: 37, 38, 39, and 40 Find the tangential and normal components of the acceleration vector.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {({t^{2} + 1})}\mathbf{i} + t^{3}\mathbf{j}$$ , $$t \geqslant 0$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = 2t^{2}\mathbf{i} + \left( {\frac{2}{3}t^{3} - 2t} \right)\mathbf{j}$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = \cos t\mathbf{i} + \sin t\mathbf{j} + t\mathbf{k}$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = t\mathbf{i} + 2e^{ t}\mathbf{j} + e^{2t}\mathbf{k}$$

exercises.instruction: 41–42 Find the tangential and normal components of the acceleration vector at the given point.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = \ln t\mathbf{i} + {({t^{2} + 3t})}\mathbf{j} + 4\sqrt{t}\mathbf{k}$$ , $$({0,4,4})$$
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = \frac{1}{t}\mathbf{i} + \frac{1}{t^{2}}\mathbf{j} + \frac{1}{t^{3}}\mathbf{k}$$ , $$({1,1,1})$$
The magnitude of the acceleration vector $$\mathbf{a}$$ is $$10{cm} \slash s^{2}$$ . Use the figure to estimate the tangential and normal components of $$\mathbf{a}$$ .

image.alt: Details A curve and a vector are graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The curve begins at the origin, goes steeply upward to the right, and concaves up. An arrowhead placed on the curve points up and slightly to the right. The vector begins from the curve, and slopes steeply upward to the left.

problem.paragraph: Angular Momentum and Torque If a particle with mass $$m$$ moves with position vector $$\mathbf{r}{(t)}$$ , then its angular momentum is defined as $$\mathbf{L}{(t)} = m\mathbf{r}{(t)} \times \mathbf{v}{(t)}$$ and its torque as $$\mathbf{\tau}{(t)} = m\mathbf{r}{(t)} \times \mathbf{a}{(t)}$$ . Show that $$\mathbf{L}^{\prime}{(t)} = \mathbf{\tau}{(t)}$$ . Deduce that if $$\mathbf{\tau}{(t)} = 0$$ for all $$t$$ , then $$\mathbf{L}{(t)}$$ is constant. (This is the law of conservation of angular momentum.)
The position function of a spacecraft is
$$\mathbf{r}{(t)} = {({3 + t})}\mathbf{i} + {({2 + \ln t})}\mathbf{j} + \left( {7 - \frac{4}{t^{2} + 1}} \right){\mathbf{k}}$$
and the coordinates of a space station are $$({6,4,9})$$ . The captain wants the craft to coast into the space station. When should the engines be turned off?

A rocket burning its onboard fuel while moving through space has velocity $$\mathbf{v}{(t)}$$ and mass $$m{(t)}$$ at time $$t$$ . If the exhaust gases escape with velocity $$\mathbf{v}_{e}$$ relative to the rocket, it can be deduced from Newton’s Second Law of Motion that
$$m\frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt} = \frac{dm}{dt}\mathbf{v}_{e}$$

list.item: For the rocket to accelerate in a straight line from rest to twice the speed of its own exhaust gases, what fraction of its initial mass would the rocket have to burn as fuel?
